title: Hiring, Developing and Strengthening Singaporean Core
what_it_is: Hiring, Developing and Strengthening Singaporean Core

sections.label: Tech@SG programme need question
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Tech@SG programme, which helps technology firms hire foreign talent, is needed given economic conditions and Singaporean Core focus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in light of the current economic conditions and our focus on hiring, developing and strengthening the Singaporean Core, whether there is a need for the Tech@SG programme which facilitates technology firms in the hiring of foreign talent.

sections.label: TechSkills Accelerator training places
sections.summary: Over 74,000 training places were taken up or committed under the TechSkills Accelerator, about one-third of ICT professionals, with over 63,000 local enrolments in tech courses in Academic Year 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Today, more than 74,000 training places have been taken up or committed under the TechSkills Accelerator and this will amount to about one-third of our information and communications technology (ICT) professionals across the country.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In Academic Year 2018, there was an enrolment of more than 63,000 locals in these tech-related courses, which received about $1.1 billion in Government funding.

sections.label: Tech@SG company funding criteria
sections.summary: Companies must have secured over US$10 million in cumulative VC funding and received funding from a Programme-recognised VC in the past 36 months, enabling globally competitive teams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Companies would also need to have secured more than US$10 million in Venture Capital (VC) funding cumulatively and have received funding from a Programme-recognised VC in the past 36 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Tech@SG will enable such companies to put together globally competitive teams to develop their products and internationalise quickly.

sections.label: First semiconductor companies jobs
sections.summary: In three years, Singapore's first three semiconductor companies, National Semiconductor, Fairchild and Texas Instruments, created more than 7,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In a span of just three years, the first three semiconductor companies in Singapore – National Semiconductor, Fairchild and Texas Instruments – created more than 7,000 jobs.

sections.label: Mastercard Graduate Programme for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The company introduced the Mastercard Graduate Programme offering Singaporean employees structured rotations, international work experience and mentorship opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To that end, the company introduced the Mastercard Graduate Programme that offers Singaporean employees a structured programme of rotations, international work experience and mentorship opportunities.

sections.label: Fair Consideration Framework application
sections.summary: The Fair Consideration Framework applies to everyone and every firm in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Fair Consideration Framework applies to everyone and every firm in Singapore.

sections.label: Economy average growth varies by sector
sections.summary: The economy's average growth may be about 0% to 1%, but not every sector grows between 0% and 1%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: At this point in time, the average of the economy may be about 0% to 1% growth, but that does not mean that every sector is between 0% and 1% growth.

sections.label: China's 千人计划 talent competition
sections.summary: China, the most populous country, has a 千人计划 to attract the world's best back to China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Just to put in context how tough this competition is, China, the most populous country in the world, even China has a 千人计划 to attract the best from around the world to go back to China and help.

sections.label: Localising financial sector expertise
sections.summary: Singapore brought in globally attuned experts, then progressively localised expertise, achieving much under the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: When we grew our financial sector, there will obviously be areas where we initially lack the expertise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We brought in people and experts who are globally attuned and have the exposure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Over time, we progressively make sure that that expertise is localised and we have achieved much in the financial sector, under the leadership of the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

sections.label: Fair Consideration Framework and localising talent
sections.summary: The Fair Consideration Framework, called the 'triple-weak' by Mr Patrick Tay, ensures companies localise talent and build Singapore capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is why, just now, in answering Mr Patrick Tay's question, I talked about the Fair Consideration Framework, what Mr Patrick Tay called the "triple-weak".

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We want to make sure that every company, as they grow, are conscious of their responsibility to localise the talent and also to build up the capabilities within Singapore.
